name: KY-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: District partisan lean of R+32 makes this one of the most Republican seats in the country
Incumbent Hal Rogers runs with a large cash advantage, about $875,000 on hand versus $143,000 for Democrat Ned Pillersdorf
Prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; even a favorable national environment falls far short of what this district would require
model.rationale: A 32-point Republican partisan lean, an entrenched incumbent seeking another term, and a decisive fundraising edge leave Pillersdorf without a plausible path in this general election. Markets and fundamentals point the same direction, and nothing in the money or campaign picture suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Only a major late-breaking scandal or health issue involving Rogers, combined with a historic national wave, could narrow the margin, and even that would likely leave the seat in Republican hands.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kentucky's fifth district is among the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 32 points toward the GOP. Hal Rogers, the long-time incumbent, is seeking another term and enters the general election with a large financial edge: about $875,000 on hand compared with roughly $143,000 for Democrat Ned Pillersdorf. Two independents, Gerardo Serrano and Mikel Wein, are also on the ballot but have raised little or nothing.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 97 percent. Even a strong national Democratic environment would need to move the district by an enormous margin to put the seat in play, and nothing in the fundraising or campaign signals suggests a shift of that scale. The seat remains safely in Republican hands.
